said: Sat Feb 1: 25% tariffs on Canada and Mexico, 10% on China, starting Tuesday.
did: Paused Mexico and Canada for 30 days on the Monday itself.
context: Stocks fell early, then pared losses as the Mexico pause came out.
headline: Canada/Mexico tariffs, paused same day

said: "No room left" for a deal: 25% tariffs on Canada and Mexico start tomorrow.
did: Did it. The tariffs took effect Mar 4; China's rate rose to 20%.
context: A weak ISM manufacturing survey the same morning.
headline: "No room left": tariffs go live

said: Asked on Fox about a 2025 recession: "I hate to predict things like that. There is a period of transition."
did: A hedge, not a policy. Commerce Sec. Lutnick said there was "no chance" of a recession the same weekend.
context: Weak economic data and a Delta profit warning landed the same day.
headline: "Period of transition" recession hedge

said: "Liberation Day" (Apr 2, after the close): 10% global baseline tariff plus reciprocal rates of 11–50%.
did: Did it. The 10% baseline took effect Apr 5.
context: None major. Kobeissi: futures lost ~$2T in under 15 minutes as he read the list.
headline: Liberation Day tariffs

said: Held firm on the Apr 2 tariffs as China retaliated with 34% on all US goods.
did: Did it: the tariffs stayed on. Two-day loss of 10.5%, the 5th biggest since 1950.
context: China's retaliation drove the second day.
headline: Holds firm as China retaliates

said: Nothing. A false headline said adviser Hassett claimed Trump was considering a 90-day pause.
did: Never happened. The White House called it "FAKE NEWS" and CNBC/Reuters issued corrections.
context: S&P went from -4.7% to +3.4% intraday, then closed -0.2%. Kobeissi called it the biggest 30-minute market-cap swing ever.
headline: Fake 90-day pause headline

said: 9:37am: "THIS IS A GREAT TIME TO BUY!!! DJT". Then a 90-day pause with a 10% rate for most countries; China raised to 125%.
did: Walked back his own tariffs after weeks of saying there'd be no delay.
context: A bond-market selloff the night before. Best day since 2008.
headline: "Great time to buy" → 90-day pause

said: Truth Social: the economy could slow unless "Mr. Too Late, a major loser" cuts rates NOW.
did: Powell was not fired. Hassett said the administration was studying it; rates were not cut that week.
context: Dollar hit a 3-year low (the "Sell America" trade).
headline: "Mr. Too Late" attack on Powell

said: Geneva truce: US tariffs on China cut from 145% to 30% for 90 days; China's cut from 125% to 10%.
did: Did it. The cuts started May 14.
context: PPI and retail sales data due the same week.
headline: China truce: 145% → 30%

said: EU talks "going nowhere": a 50% EU tariff from June 1, plus 25% on iPhones made abroad.
did: Walked back. He delayed the EU tariff to July 9 two days later.
context: Apple fell about 3% on the iPhone threat.
headline: 50% EU + iPhone tariff threat

said: Fri May 23: a "straight 50% Tariff" on the EU from June 1. Sun May 25: delayed to July 9.
did: Walked back within 48 hours. The FT's "TACO" (Trump Always Chickens Out) trade got its name here.
context: A better-than-expected consumer confidence report.
headline: EU 50% tariff delayed

said: Tariff letters: 25% on Japan and South Korea, up to 40% on others, from Aug 1.
did: Did it. The new rates rolled out Aug 1 (see Aug 1).
context: Tesla fell 6.8% on the Musk-Trump feud.
headline: Tariff letters to Japan, Korea

said: New tariff rates on dozens of countries; then fired the BLS chief, calling the jobs data "rigged".
did: Did it. The tariffs rolled out and the commissioner was fired.
context: A weak jobs report (73k jobs) and Amazon earnings hit the same day.
headline: Tariffs roll out, BLS chief fired

said: Threatened a "massive increase" in China tariffs over rare earths, then 100% on top of existing tariffs from Nov 1.
did: Softened two days later (see Oct 13).
context: Stocks were near records after a calm stretch.
headline: 100% China tariff threat

said: "Don't worry about China, it will all be fine!" He said Xi "just had a bad moment."
did: Walked back the Oct 10 threat.
context: Broadcom jumped 9.9% on an OpenAI deal.
headline: "Don't worry about China"

said: 10% tariffs from Feb 1 (25% from June 1) on 8 European countries until a deal for the "Complete and Total purchase of Greenland."
did: Cancelled the next day (see Jan 21).
context: Japanese bond yields hit record highs. First trading day after MLK Day.
headline: Greenland tariffs on 8 countries

said: Ruled out force in his Davos speech, then posted: "I will not be imposing the Tariffs" after a Greenland "framework" with NATO.
did: Walked back. No signed deal; the framework had few details.
context: None major.
headline: Greenland tariffs dropped

said: Not his move: the Supreme Court ruled 6–3 that IEEPA doesn't authorize tariffs. He vowed replacement duties.
did: Overruled by the court; replacement tariffs under another law.
context: Q4 GDP came in at 1.4% vs 2.5% expected the same morning.
headline: Supreme Court kills IEEPA tariffs

said: Sat Feb 28: announced "major combat operations" against Iran with Israel.
did: Did it. Iran moved to close the Strait of Hormuz and oil jumped.
context: Closed essentially flat; energy and defense stocks offset the selloff. A strong ISM report helped.
headline: Strikes on Iran begin

said: Told CBS: "I think the war is very complete, pretty much."
did: Didn't check out. Fighting went on until an Apr 7 ceasefire; S&P fell 5.1% in March.
context: Oil had spiked near $120 that morning. S&P went from -1.5% to +0.8% in the last hour.
headline: "War is very complete"

said: Reports said he'd end the war without a full Strait of Hormuz reopening; an unconfirmed rumor said Iran was open to talks.
did: Unconfirmed at the time. A ceasefire came a week later.
context: Quarter-end. Best day since May 2025.
headline: Reports he'd end the war

said: Announced a two-week ceasefire less than 90 minutes before his own Hormuz deadline.
did: Did it. The S&P hit a record a week later.
context: Oil fell below $95.
headline: Iran ceasefire

said: Extended the ceasefire indefinitely at Pakistan's request.
did: Did it, though the US naval blockade of Iran's ports stayed in place.
context: Earnings season; chip stocks hit records.
headline: Ceasefire extended

said: Said he thinks the agreement with Iran is "over" amid an exchange of strikes.
did: Strikes resumed. Brent rose 6% to about $79, but the S&P barely moved.
context: The Dow fell 1% while the S&P held.
headline: "Agreement is over"
